faq.gettingStarted.q1.q.message: What does Simple JWT Login do?

faq.gettingStarted.q1.a.message: It adds JWT authentication to the WordPress REST API. Apps can log users in, register them, reset passwords, and call any REST endpoint as that user, all configured from wp-admin.

faq.gettingStarted.q2.a.message: No. Every feature is in the free version, under GPLv3, with no paid plan or add-on to buy.

faq.gettingStarted.q3.q.message: Which WordPress and PHP versions are supported?

faq.gettingStarted.q3.a.message: WordPress 6.2 and later. The plugin code runs on PHP 5.5 to 8.5, but in practice your PHP version is set by the WordPress version you run.

faq.gettingStarted.q4.q.message: Why does every endpoint return "not enabled" after I install it?

faq.gettingStarted.q4.a.message: Every plugin endpoint starts disabled, so you expose only what you need. Turn on Allow JWT Authentication, and any other feature you use, in the plugin settings.

faq.loggingIn.q1.q.message: Can users log in with a username instead of an email?

faq.loggingIn.q1.a.message: Yes. Send email, username, or login, which accepts either one, together with the password.

faq.loggingIn.q2.q.message: Can users log in with Google, Facebook, GitHub, or Auth0?

faq.loggingIn.q2.a.message: Yes. The app exchanges the provider token for a WordPress JWT, and the plugin can create the WordPress user on the first login.

faq.loggingIn.q3.a.message: Yes. With the Two Factor plugin installed, users who set up 2FA get a short-lived interim token and must pass the second step before they receive the full JWT.

faq.loggingIn.q4.q.message: How do I use the JWT on WordPress core endpoints such as /wp/v2/posts?

faq.loggingIn.q4.a.message: Turn on JWT Middleware for all WordPress endpoints. WordPress then treats any REST request with a valid JWT as coming from that user.

faq.tokens.q1.q.message: How long does a JWT last?

faq.tokens.q1.a.message: 60 minutes by default. You can change the expiry in the Authentication settings. Keep it short and use refresh tokens to keep users logged in.

faq.tokens.q2.q.message: How do I keep users logged in after the JWT expires?

faq.tokens.q2.a.message: Turn on refresh tokens. The login response then includes a `refresh_token`, which the app exchanges for a new JWT before or after the old one expires.

faq.tokens.q3.q.message: How do I log a user out?

faq.tokens.q3.a.message: Revoke the JWT. A revoked token is rejected even if it has not expired yet.

faq.tokens.q4.q.message: Can I add custom data to the JWT?

faq.tokens.q4.a.message: Yes. Choose the claims in the Authentication settings, or add your own with the `simple_jwt_login_jwt_payload_auth` filter.

faq.tokens.q5.q.message: Where is the signing key stored?

faq.tokens.q5.a.message: In the plugin settings by default. To keep it out of the database, define `SIMPLE_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY` in `wp-config.php` instead.

faq.security.q1.q.message: Should servers and scripts use a JWT?

faq.security.q1.a.message: Use an API key instead. API keys are long-lived, scoped to read, create, update, or delete, and can be revoked at any time.

faq.security.q2.q.message: How do I require a JWT on a REST route?

faq.security.q2.a.message: Add a rule in Protect Endpoints. Requests to that route without a valid JWT are rejected.

faq.security.q3.q.message: How do I report a security vulnerability?

faq.security.q3.a.message: Report it privately through GitHub security advisories, never in a public issue or forum.

faq.troubleshooting.q1.q.message: Why is my JWT ignored even though I send it?

faq.troubleshooting.q1.a.message: The web server most likely strips the Authorization header before it reaches PHP. Send the token in another header, such as `X-Token`, or fix the server configuration.

faq.troubleshooting.q2.q.message: Why does my browser app get a CORS error?

faq.troubleshooting.q2.a.message: Add the app origin to Allow origin in the CORS settings, and Authorization to Allow headers. Since version 4.1.1, a JWT from another site is trusted only when its origin is listed. A `*` entry trusts the `Authorization` header, but never cookie or session JWTs.

faq.troubleshooting.q3.q.message: What does an error code mean?

faq.troubleshooting.q3.a.message: Every error response includes an `error_code`. The error codes page explains each one and how to fix it.

headlessWordpress.faq.q1.a.message: Headless WordPress uses WordPress to manage content and users, while a separate front end, such as a Next.js site or a mobile app, shows it. The two communicate through the REST API or GraphQL.

headlessWordpress.faq.q2.q.message: Why use JWT authentication with headless WordPress?

headlessWordpress.faq.q2.a.message: WordPress login cookies are made for pages that WordPress serves. A JWT is a signed token that any client can send with a request, so it also works for separate front ends, mobile apps, and servers.

headlessWordpress.faq.q3.q.message: Does it work with WooCommerce and WPGraphQL?

headlessWordpress.faq.q3.a.message: Yes. The same JWT can authenticate the WooCommerce REST and Store APIs and WPGraphQL requests.

headlessWordpress.faq.q4.q.message: Where should the front end store the JWT?

headlessWordpress.faq.q4.a.message: For websites, keep it in an HttpOnly cookie set by your server. For mobile apps, use the secure storage of the device. Avoid browser local storage for sensitive apps.

headlessWordpress.faq.q5.a.message: Yes. It is free and open-source, forever, with no paid tier.

homepage.jsonLd.description.message: Free, open-source WordPress plugin that adds JWT authentication to the WordPress REST API. Supports login, register, auto-login, endpoint protection, token refresh, and more.

homepage.features.autologin.description.message: Open a WordPress session from a JWT link - for example, send a renewal email that lands the member on their account page, already logged in.

homepage.features.register.description.message: Create WordPress users from a mobile sign-up screen, and limit who can register by Auth Code, IP, or email domain.

homepage.features.delete.description.message: Offer an account deletion button in your app. The JWT identifies the account to remove.

homepage.features.authenticate.descripti.message: Exchange WordPress credentials for a JWT, then refresh, validate, or revoke it - the login flow for a React or mobile app.

homepage.features.resetPassword.descript.message: Build a "Forgot password" screen in your app: email a reset code, then set the new password through the REST API.

homepage.features.limitIp.description.message: Accept logins or registrations only from your backend or office network - wildcards such as {code} work too.

homepage.features.roles.description.message: Tie a role to each Auth Code - for example, one code for free members and another for premium - on a single endpoint.

homepage.features.plugins.description.message: Send login links from MailPoet, authorize WPGraphQL queries, or call the REST routes that other plugins add.

homepage.features.protectEndpoints.descr.message: Require a JWT or a role per route and HTTP method - for example, stop anonymous visitors from listing {code}.

homepage.features.jwtAnyEndpoint.descrip.message: Publish a post to {code} from a mobile app as the logged-in author, without session cookies.

homepage.features.googleOauth.descriptio.message: Add Google sign-in to your front end and get a WordPress JWT back, so users have no extra password to remember.

homepage.features.googleJwt.title.message: Use Google JWT on All Endpoints

homepage.features.googleJwt.description.message: Already use Google sign-in in your app? Send the Google-issued token directly to WordPress REST endpoints.

homepage.features.apiKeys.description.message: Give a CI pipeline a key that can only read and create content, with an expiry date you choose.

homepage.features.oauthProviders.title.message: Sign In with Auth0, Facebook & GitHub

homepage.features.oauthProviders.descrip.message: Use the identity provider you already have: exchange an Auth0, Facebook, or GitHub login for a WordPress JWT.

homepage.features.oauthProviders.alt.message: OAuth with Auth0, Facebook, and GitHub

homepage.features.twoFactor.description.message: A stolen password alone gets no JWT: users with 2FA in the WordPress Two Factor plugin must also enter their code.

homepage.features.auditLogs.description.message: Find out who deleted an account or why a login failed - search authentication events in wp-admin.

homepage.features.webhooks.description.message: Post to Slack when a user registers, or forward authentication events to your logging service.

homepage.features.woocommerce.descriptio.message: Build a React storefront: manage products and run the cart & checkout through the WooCommerce REST and Store APIs.

homepage.features.multipleKeys.descripti.message: Accept Auth0 tokens next to your own, or rotate keys in stages - rules pick the key from a JWT header or payload claim.

homepage.features.jwtDecoder.description.message: Debug a rejected token without pasting it into a third-party site: read its header and payload in wp-admin.

homepage.security.off.desc.message: Every plugin endpoint starts disabled. You expose only the operations your app needs.

homepage.security.csrf.desc.message: Cookie and session JWTs are ignored on cross-site requests unless you list that exact origin, which blocks CSRF.

homepage.security.tokens.desc.message: Refresh tokens rotate on every use, JWTs can be revoked, and an optional setting ends sessions when a password changes.

homepage.security.keys.desc.message: API keys are stored only as SHA-256 hashes. Permissions follow the dispatched method, so method overrides cannot raise them.

homepage.security.fixes.desc.message: Reported vulnerabilities are fixed and shipped in regular releases, documented in the release notes.

homepage.security.tests.desc.message: A dedicated security test suite covers CSRF, user enumeration, trusted proxy IPs and ambient credentials, so fixed issues stay fixed.

homepage.security.ci.desc.message: Unit, feature and cross-site test suites run automatically in GitHub Actions.

homepage.security.wpCompat.desc.message: Feature tests run against a real WordPress install, alongside PHP syntax checks across multiple PHP versions and the official WordPress Plugin Check.

homepage.security.disclosure.desc.message: Found a vulnerability? Report it privately through GitHub security advisories instead of opening a public issue, so a fix can ship before details go public.

homepage.meta.description.message: Simple JWT Login is a free, open-source WordPress plugin that adds JWT authentication to the REST API - no coding required.

homepage.hero.subtitle.message: JWT login, registration, and endpoint protection for the WordPress REST API -{br}for headless sites, mobile apps, and WPGraphQL. Configured from wp-admin.

homepage.v4Banner.text.message: Simple JWT Login v4 is now available - API Keys, 2FA, Audit Logs, Webhooks, and more. v3 is now in maintenance mode (EOL Jan 31, 2027).

homepage.features.title.message: From first login to token revocation

homepage.features.lead.message: Each feature is tagged {v3} or {v4} depending on which version introduced it.

homepage.why.title.message: Why developers choose Simple JWT Login

homepage.why.noCoding.desc.message: Keys, expiration, allowed IPs, and protected routes are all settings in wp-admin.

homepage.why.algorithms.desc.message: Sign with a shared secret (HS256/384/512), or use RS256/384/512 so other services can verify tokens with only the public key.

homepage.why.delivery.desc.message: Authorization header, cookie, session, or request parameter. Turn off the ones your app does not use.

homepage.why.developers.desc.message: Action and filter hooks let you add JWT claims, block a login, or change an API response from your own plugin.

homepage.why.cors.desc.message: List the exact front-end origins that can call your API, so a React or Vue app on another domain can log users in.

homepage.why.php.desc.message: The plugin code runs on PHP 5.5+, so your WordPress version sets the minimum. PHP 8.2 or newer is recommended in production.

homepage.why.autologin.desc.message: Put a short-lived JWT in an email link and the subscriber lands on the page already logged in.

homepage.why.lifecycle.desc.message: Keep a mobile user signed in with refresh tokens, and revoke the JWT when they log out.

homepage.why.free.desc.message: GPL 3.0 licensed, free and open-source, forever. No paid tier and no locked features.

homepage.security.lead.message: A login plugin guards your whole site. Here is how the latest v4 release limits what an attacker can do, and how the project tests and fixes it - each card links to the details.

homepage.ecosystem.title.message: SDKs and integrations for PHP, JavaScript, WPGraphQL, and WP-CLI

homepage.ecosystem.php.desc.message: Connect any PHP app to Simple JWT Login with one Composer package - supports Laravel, Yii, CodeIgniter, and more.

homepage.ecosystem.js.desc.message: Add JWT authentication to React, Vue, Angular, or any JS app with an npm package and a handful of lines.

homepage.ecosystem.wpgraphql.desc.message: Use your JWTs to authenticate GraphQL queries and mutations - enable it with a single checkbox.

homepage.ecosystem.mailpoet.desc.message: Send magic-link login emails via MailPoet - let subscribers log in with one click, no password required.

homepage.ecosystem.exportImport.desc.message: Back up and restore your entire plugin configuration in one click - perfect for staging-to-production migrations.

homepage.ecosystem.cli.desc.message: Generate tokens, validate JWTs, revoke sessions, and manage every setting from your terminal - ideal for CI/CD.

homepage.demos.title.message: Try the API against your own site

homepage.demos.lead.message: Run live demos right in your browser, against your own WordPress site - nothing is sent anywhere except the URL you provide.

homepage.deploy.title.message: Don't have a site yet? Launch one in one click

homepage.deploy.text.message: Spin up a fully installed WordPress server on DigitalOcean - with Simple JWT Login ready for headless and REST API authentication. No Marketplace setup, no terminal, no install wizard. We hand you the login.

homepage.quickStart.install.desc.message: Search for Simple JWT Login in the WordPress plugin directory, install, and activate in one click.

homepage.quickStart.configure.desc.message: Set a JWT secret key, enable the endpoints you need (all are off by default), and choose how long tokens live.

homepage.quickStart.send.desc.message: Call POST /auth to get a JWT, then send it as a Bearer token to the WordPress REST API endpoints you enable.

v4.features.apiKeys.desc.message: Create long-lived, scoped credentials for server-to-server integrations, CI/CD pipelines, and third-party services - no JWT expiry management needed.

v4.features.apiKeys.bullet1.message: Scoped permissions: read, create, update, delete

v4.features.apiKeys.bullet2.message: SHA-256 hashed - the key is never stored in plain text

v4.features.apiKeys.bullet3.message: Revoke or expire keys at any time

v4.features.apiKeys.bullet4.message: JWT authentication also accepted on the /api-keys endpoint

v4.features.apiKeys.bullet5.message: Non-admin users can manage their own keys without admin access

v4.features.oauth.desc.message: Users can sign in with Google, Auth0, Facebook, or GitHub and receive a WordPress JWT - no password form required.

v4.features.oauth.bullet1.message: Google: authorization code or ID token (Sign In With Google)

v4.features.oauth.bullet5.message: Auto-register users if no matching account exists

v4.features.multiKeys.desc.message: Define multiple decryption keys and let the plugin pick the right one automatically based on the JWT header or payload.

v4.features.multiKeys.bullet1.message: Key selection based on JWT header or payload field

v4.features.multiKeys.bullet2.message: Supports HS256/384/512 and RS256/384/512 per key

v4.features.multiKeys.bullet3.message: Seamless key rotation without breaking existing tokens

v4.features.auditLogs.desc.message: Every authentication event - logins, token issues, revocations, and errors - is now logged for auditing and debugging.

v4.features.auditLogs.bullet1.message: Logs login, register, delete, OAuth, 2FA, and token events

v4.features.webhooks.desc.message: Fire HTTP callbacks on authentication events - integrate with Slack, logging services, or any external system in real time.

v4.features.webhooks.bullet2.message: Custom URL, method, headers, and JSON payload

v4.features.dashboard.desc.message: A new at-a-glance status page shows every feature's state in one place - routes, security, integrations, and monitoring.

v4.features.dashboard.bullet1.message: All routes and their enabled/disabled state

v4.features.dashboard.bullet2.message: Security - CORS, Protect Endpoints, Auth Codes, API Keys

v4.features.dashboard.bullet3.message: Monitoring - Webhooks, Webhook Logs, Audit Logs

v4.features.settingsUi.desc.message: The plugin admin panel has been fully redesigned - cleaner layout, better grouping, and less noise so you can find what you need faster.

v4.features.settingsUi.bullet1.message: Reorganized sections for a more logical flow

v4.features.settingsUi.bullet2.message: User identification consolidated in General settings

v4.features.settingsUi.bullet3.message: Cleaner forms with improved field descriptions

v4.features.twoFa.desc.message: Require a second authentication step before issuing a full JWT - compatible with the WordPress Two Factor plugin.

v4.features.twoFa.bullet1.message: Interim JWT issued after password check; 2FA code completes the flow

v4.features.woocommerce.desc.message: Drive a WooCommerce store with a JWT instead of a consumer key/secret - manage products and run a fully headless cart & checkout with the token alone.

v4.features.woocommerce.bullet1.message: JWT auth on every /wc/ route: CRUD (wc/v3) and the Store API (wc/store)

v4.features.woocommerce.bullet2.message: Scoped to WooCommerce routes - works even with the global middleware off

v4.features.woocommerce.bullet3.message: Optional Store API cart & checkout: header-JWT requests skip the CSRF nonce

v4.features.woocommerce.bullet4.message: Admin / Shop Manager tokens manage the catalog; customers manage their own cart

v4.features.refreshToken.desc.message: Refresh tokens are now more secure and configurable - rolling rotation, a separate encryption key, and custom payload support.

v4.features.refreshToken.bullet1.message: Rolling rotation: each refresh issues a new token and invalidates the old one

v4.features.refreshToken.bullet2.message: Separate refresh token secret key, independent of the JWT signing key

v4.features.refreshToken.bullet3.message: Custom payload merged into the newly issued JWT on refresh

v4.features.refreshToken.bullet4.message: Auth Code protection option for the refresh endpoint

v4.features.jwtDecoder.desc.message: Paste any JWT directly in the WordPress admin panel to inspect its header and payload - no external tools needed.

v4.features.jwtDecoder.bullet1.message: Decodes header and payload instantly in the browser

v4.features.jwtDecoder.bullet2.message: Token is never sent to the server

v4.features.jwtDecoder.bullet3.message: Useful for debugging token claims and expiry

v4.features.codeExamples.desc.message: Every endpoint page in the plugin admin panel now shows ready-to-copy code snippets tailored to your current settings.

v4.features.codeExamples.bullet1.message: cURL, PHP, and JavaScript examples per endpoint

v4.features.codeExamples.bullet2.message: Examples use your configured namespace and site URL

v4.features.codeExamples.bullet3.message: Auth Code and parameter values pre-filled from your settings

v4.features.protectEndpoints.desc.message: Protect Endpoints has been rethought as a single ordered rules table - each rule sets access to Public, JWT required, or JWT + Roles, and the first matching rule wins.

v4.features.protectEndpoints.bullet1.message: Unified rules table replaces separate whitelist and protected lists

v4.features.protectEndpoints.bullet2.message: Per-rule access level - Public, JWT required, or JWT + specific Roles

v4.features.protectEndpoints.bullet4.message: Existing settings auto-migrate on first load

v4.features.protectEndpoints.bullet5.message: Role names are validated against WordPress on save

v4.features.registration.desc.message: User registration is now more flexible - assign multiple default roles, trigger built-in WordPress notification emails, and use variables in reset password email subjects.

v4.features.registration.bullet1.message: Support multiple default user roles on registration

v4.features.registration.bullet2.message: Option to send the default WordPress welcome email on registration

v4.features.registration.bullet3.message: Option to send the default WordPress password-changed email from the change-password endpoint

v4.features.registration.bullet4.message: Variables now supported in the reset password email subject line

v4.features.tokenControls.desc.message: Enable or disable refresh, revoke, and validate token endpoints independently - ship only the surface area your app needs.

v4.features.tokenControls.bullet4.message: Optionally require the "Bearer" prefix in the Authorization header

v4.features.improvements.desc.message: Standardized HTTP status codes across all endpoints and a cleaner, more maintainable internal codebase.

v4.features.improvements.bullet1.message: Client errors return a matching HTTP status (400, 401, 403, 404, 422, or 429) instead of 500 - 404 and 429 since 4.2.0

v4.features.improvements.bullet2.message: Refactored internal service layer for better separation of concerns

v4.features.improvements.bullet3.message: Improved unit test coverage across all core services

v4.features.improvements.bullet4.message: Reduced code duplication across service classes

v4.breaking.registerResponse.detail.message: {postUsers} used to return {oldShape}. It now returns {newShape}. The user fields and roles are nested under {data}, {message} is gone, and these fields were renamed: {userLogin} → {login}, {userNicename} → {nicename}, {userEmail} → {email}, {userUrl} → {url}, {userRegistered} → {registered}, {userStatus} → {status}.

v4.breaking.registerResponse.action.message: Update any code that reads user fields from the register response - check both the new nesting under {data} and the renamed field keys.

v4.breaking.legacyRegister.detail.message: The old POST /simple-jwt-login/v1/register route no longer exists. The canonical route is POST /simple-jwt-login/v1/users.

v4.breaking.legacyRegister.action.message: Update all callers to use POST /simple-jwt-login/v1/users.

v4.breaking.userIdentification.title.message: User Identification moved to General settings

v4.breaking.userIdentification.detail.message: The "User Identification" option (email, login, ID) has moved from the Delete User settings tab to the General settings tab. It now applies globally to all endpoints.

v4.breaking.userIdentification.action.message: After upgrading, verify the User Identification value in Settings → Simple JWT Login → General.

v4.breaking.settingsStorage.detail.message: The internal layout of plugin options in {wpOptions} has changed. Existing settings are migrated automatically on first load, but the old keys are removed.

v4.breaking.settingsStorage.action.message: Review every settings tab after upgrading to confirm values carried over correctly.

v4.breaking.authRefreshToken.detail.message: {postAuth} returns a new {refreshToken} field when the refresh token feature is enabled. The JWT field itself is unchanged.

v4.breaking.authRefreshToken.action.message: No action needed unless your client strictly rejects unexpected response fields or you need to store the token.

v4.breaking.twoFa.title.message: 2FA changes the /auth flow for affected users

v4.breaking.twoFa.detail.message: Users with the Two Factor plugin configured now receive a short-lived interim JWT from /auth instead of a full JWT. A second request to POST /auth/2fa (with the interim JWT + 2FA code) is required to get the real token.

v4.breaking.twoFa.action.message: Update your authentication flow to handle the interim JWT case, or leave 2FA disabled for API users.

v4.breaking.protectedStatus.title.message: Protected endpoint auth failures return 401 instead of 403

v4.breaking.protectedStatus.detail.message: When the Protect Endpoint feature blocks an unauthenticated request, the plugin previously returned HTTP 403 Forbidden. It now returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized to align with the HTTP spec.

v4.breaking.protectedStatus.action.message: Update any code that checks specifically for status 403 on protected routes to handle 401 instead.

v4.breaking.errorField.detail.message: In v3, the error field in responses was named {errorCode} (camelCase). In v4, it is renamed to {errorCodeSnake} (snake_case) to match the naming convention used across the API.

v4.breaking.errorField.action.message: Update all error-handling code that reads {respErrorCode} (or {respDataErrorCode}) to use {errorCodeSnake} instead.

v4.support.v4.desc.message: New features, bug fixes, security patches, and WordPress compatibility fixes.

v4.support.v3.desc.message: Security patches and WordPress compatibility fixes only - no new features, no bug fixes. End of life is January 31, 2027.

v4.migration.step1.desc.message: Download the plugin from GitHub and upload the zip via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, or install it from the WordPress plugin directory.

v4.migration.step2.desc.message: The breaking changes are listed above. Address them before going to production - the {errorCode} → {errorCodeSnake} rename, the register response shape change, the removed /register route, and the relocated User Identification setting are the most likely to affect existing integrations. The {upgradeGuide} covers every change, including those from later 4.x releases.

v4.migration.step3.desc.message: Your settings are automatically migrated. Open Settings → Simple JWT Login and verify your values carried over correctly.

v4.migration.step4.desc.message: Enable API Keys, Webhooks, Audit Logs, 2FA, and the 4 OAuth providers from Settings → Simple JWT Login to start using the new capabilities.

demos.todo.notice.message: {before} on your WordPress site: enable {allowAuth}, turn on {allEndpoints} (so {postsCode} accepts the token), and enable CORS for this origin. See the {guideLink}.

demos.todo.notice.allEndpoints.message: All WordPress endpoints check for JWT

demos.todo.privacy.message: {strong} This website does not store any data you enter in the live example - your WordPress URL, credentials, and any details you submit are kept in your browser and sent only to your own WordPress site.

demos.userManagement.privacy.message: {strong} This website does not store any data you enter in the live example - your WordPress URL, credentials, and any details you submit are kept in your browser and sent only to your own WordPress site.

demos.woocommerce.notice.message: {before} on your WordPress site: activate WooCommerce (with a payment method such as Cash on Delivery), enable the {integrationLink} and its {storeApi} toggle, and enable CORS for this origin. ecosystem.cli.commands.login.description.message: Authenticate any WordPress user by username, email, or a combined login flag and receive a signed JWT immediately. Pipe it directly into curl, store it in a variable, or forward it to other tools.

ecosystem.cli.commands.decode.descriptio.message: Decode any JWT and display its claims as a readable key/value table or JSON. Signature is not verified - use validate for that. Perfect for debugging token contents without a browser.

ecosystem.cli.commands.validate.descript.message: Verify the token signature against the plugin decryption key and confirm it has not expired. Exits 0 in all cases - check the valid field in the output to drive conditional logic in scripts.

ecosystem.cli.commands.revoke.descriptio.message: Revoke a token so it can never be used again. The signature is verified before revocation to prevent spoofed revocation attempts. Ideal for forced log-out flows and post-deployment security sweeps.

ecosystem.cli.commands.config.descriptio.message: Get, set, list, export, and import every Simple JWT Login setting without touching the WordPress admin UI. Use dot notation for nested keys. Export/import enables reproducible config across environments.

ecosystem.cli.useCases.ciCd.description.message: Generate a short-lived JWT inside your pipeline to seed test data, run authenticated smoke tests, or hit protected API endpoints - no browser, no cookies.

ecosystem.cli.useCases.migration.descrip.message: Export the full plugin config from staging with one command, preview the diff on production in dry-run mode, then apply - fully non-interactive.

ecosystem.cli.useCases.healthChecks.desc.message: Add a cron job or monitoring script that logs in, validates the token, and alerts your team when JWT authentication breaks.

ecosystem.cli.meta.description.message: Manage Simple JWT Login from the command line - generate tokens, validate JWTs, revoke sessions, and configure the plugin.

ecosystem.cli.hero.subtitle.message: Generate tokens, validate JWTs, revoke sessions, and manage every plugin setting directly from your terminal - no WordPress admin UI required.

ecosystem.exportImport.install.core.desc.message: Make sure the core plugin is installed and active on all WordPress sites involved.

ecosystem.exportImport.install.download..message: Grab the zip from GitHub and upload it via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin on each site.

ecosystem.exportImport.install.export.de.message: On the source site go to Simple JWT Login settings and click Export. Save the generated JSON.

ecosystem.exportImport.install.import.de.message: On the destination site paste the JSON into the Import field, review the diff, and confirm.

ecosystem.exportImport.cta.subtitle.message: Install the free Export-Import add-on and move your complete Simple JWT Login setup to any site in seconds.

ecosystem.index.addons.cli.description.message: Manage Simple JWT Login without ever opening the WordPress admin. Generate tokens, validate JWTs, revoke sessions, and push config between environments - all scriptable, all automatable.

ecosystem.index.addons.mailpoet.descript.message: Drop a shortcode into any MailPoet campaign and every subscriber gets a personalized, one-click login link. No passwords, no friction - just a seamless email-to-site experience.

ecosystem.index.addons.exportImport.tagl.message: Move your config in one command

ecosystem.index.addons.exportImport.desc.message: Back up your complete Simple JWT Login configuration - Auth Codes, protection rules, and all settings - and restore it on any site. Ideal for staging migrations and multi-site setups.

ecosystem.index.integrations.wpgraphql.d.message: Use the same JWTs you issue through Simple JWT Login to authenticate any WPGraphQL query or mutation. Enable it with a single checkbox - no code, no custom middleware.

ecosystem.index.integrations.google.desc.message: Let users authenticate with their Google Account. Simple JWT Login exchanges a Google ID token for a WordPress JWT, giving you full control over the session without storing passwords.

ecosystem.index.integrations.google.high.message: Use Google JWT on all endpoints

ecosystem.index.sdks.php.tagline.message: One Composer package, any PHP framework

ecosystem.index.sdks.php.description.message: Integrate Simple JWT Login into any PHP app with a single dependency. Works out of the box with Laravel, Yii, CodeIgniter, Slim, and plain PHP.

ecosystem.index.sdks.js.tagline.message: npm package for any JS framework

ecosystem.index.sdks.js.description.message: Add Simple JWT Login authentication to React, Vue, Angular, or any JavaScript app with a handful of lines. Works in the browser and in Node.js.

ecosystem.index.meta.description.message: Explore every add-on, integration, and SDK for Simple JWT Login - WP-CLI, Google OAuth, MailPoet, WPGraphQL, PHP and JS clients.

ecosystem.index.meta.ogDescription.message: Add-ons, integrations, and SDKs that extend Simple JWT Login.

ecosystem.index.hero.subtitle.message: Add-ons, integrations, and client SDKs that bring JWT authentication to every corner of your stack - CLI pipelines, headless frontends, email campaigns, and more.

ecosystem.index.addons.lead.message: Standalone WordPress plugins that extend Simple JWT Login with new capabilities. Install them the same way you install any WordPress plugin.

ecosystem.index.integrations.lead.message: Connect Simple JWT Login to the tools you already use. Each integration is built into the core plugin - no extra downloads needed.

ecosystem.index.sdks.lead.message: Drop-in client libraries for your frontend or backend application. Available on Packagist and npm.

ecosystem.index.cta.subtitle.message: Simple JWT Login exposes 16 action and filter hooks. Build your own integration - or open an issue on GitHub and let's discuss it.

ecosystem.jsSdk.examples.auth.descriptio.message: Authenticate any WordPress user by email or username and receive a signed JWT. Store it in memory or in local storage and attach it to every subsequent request via the Authorization header.

ecosystem.jsSdk.examples.register.descri.message: Register new WordPress users from your frontend. Optionally assign a role and receive a JWT immediately - no admin UI, no custom backend code required.

ecosystem.jsSdk.examples.validate.headli.message: Verify a JWT is still valid

ecosystem.jsSdk.examples.validate.descri.message: Check that a token has not expired and its signature is intact. Call this on page load or before any protected API request to avoid unnecessary 401 errors.

ecosystem.jsSdk.examples.refresh.descrip.message: Exchange an expiring token for a fresh one without asking the user to log in again. Schedule this before expiry to maintain seamless sessions in SPAs and mobile web apps.

ecosystem.jsSdk.examples.revoke.descript.message: Permanently revoke a JWT on sign-out so it can never be reused - even if someone has a copy. Pair with clearing local storage for a complete logout flow.

ecosystem.jsSdk.useCases.react.descripti.message: Authenticate users from a React SPA or a Next.js app. Store the JWT in a context provider and attach it to every fetch or Axios call to your WordPress REST API.

ecosystem.jsSdk.useCases.vue.description.message: Integrate JWT authentication into a Vue 3 or Nuxt application. Use a Pinia store to hold the token and a composable to expose login/logout actions.

ecosystem.jsSdk.useCases.node.descriptio.message: Use the client on the server side to validate tokens in Express middleware, script WordPress user creation in CI, or build a BFF that proxies authenticated WP API calls.

ecosystem.jsSdk.meta.title.message: JavaScript Client SDK - Simple JWT Login

ecosystem.jsSdk.meta.description.message: Official JavaScript client for Simple JWT Login. Authenticate, register, validate and revoke tokens from React, Vue, Angular, or Node.js.

ecosystem.jsSdk.hero.subtitle.message: One npm package to authenticate users, manage tokens, and call the WordPress REST API from any JavaScript application - browser or Node.js.

ecosystem.jsSdk.compat.lead.message: A zero-dependency library with full ESM and CommonJS support - works in React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, or a plain script tag.

ecosystem.jsSdk.api.lead.message: Async / await API covering authentication, registration, and the full token lifecycle.

ecosystem.jsSdk.useCases.lead.message: From React SPAs to server-side Node.js middleware - the client handles the auth layer so you can focus on your application.

ecosystem.jsSdk.install.step1.desc.message: Add the package to your project.

ecosystem.jsSdk.install.step2.desc.message: Pass your WordPress site URL and Simple JWT Login Auth Code.

ecosystem.jsSdk.install.step3.desc.message: Use the async API to authenticate, register, or manage tokens.

ecosystem.jsSdk.methods.validateToken.message: Verify a token signature and expiry

ecosystem.jsSdk.methods.refreshToken.message: Get a new token from an expiring one

ecosystem.jsSdk.methods.register.message: Create a new WordPress user account

ecosystem.jsSdk.methods.delete.message: Delete a user via a verified JWT

ecosystem.jsSdk.cta.subtitle.message: One npm install and a few lines of code - that's all it takes to add WordPress JWT authentication to any JavaScript project.

ecosystem.mailpoet.jsonLd.description.message: Add magic-link login to your MailPoet email campaigns. Subscribers click once and land on your site already logged in - no password required.

ecosystem.mailpoet.params.text.desc.message: Visible link text shown to the subscriber.

ecosystem.mailpoet.params.authCode.desc.message: The Auth Code from Simple JWT Login → Auth Codes.

ecosystem.mailpoet.params.validity.desc.message: Token lifetime in seconds. Default: 604800 (1 week).

ecosystem.mailpoet.params.redirectUrl.de.message: Override the default redirect URL after login.

ecosystem.mailpoet.params.class.desc.message: CSS class(es) to apply to the link element.

ecosystem.mailpoet.params.style.desc.message: Inline CSS styles for the link.

ecosystem.mailpoet.useCases.newsletter.d.message: Include a one-click "Read your exclusive content" link in your newsletter. Subscribers land on a members-only page already logged in - no friction, higher engagement.

ecosystem.mailpoet.useCases.cart.descrip.message: Send a cart-recovery email with a magic link that logs the customer in and redirects them straight to checkout - remove every barrier between the email and the purchase.

ecosystem.mailpoet.useCases.welcome.desc.message: Welcome new members with a single click that logs them in and drops them on your onboarding page. First impressions matter - make the journey seamless from day one.

ecosystem.mailpoet.meta.description.message: Add personalized magic-link login to your MailPoet email campaigns. One shortcode, zero passwords - subscribers click and land on your site already logged in.

ecosystem.mailpoet.hero.subtitle.message: Drop one shortcode into any MailPoet template. Every subscriber gets a personalized, one-click login link - no password, no friction.

ecosystem.mailpoet.how.install.desc.message: Install the add-on, activate it, and copy your Auth Code from Simple JWT Login settings.

ecosystem.mailpoet.how.shortcode.desc.message: Drop the shortcode into any MailPoet email template. Set the link text, validity period, and redirect URL.

ecosystem.mailpoet.how.send.desc.message: MailPoet renders a unique, personalized autologin URL for each subscriber when the email is sent.

ecosystem.mailpoet.how.click.desc.message: One click logs them in and redirects them to any page on your site. No passwords, no forms.

ecosystem.mailpoet.ref.lead.message: All available parameters for the {code} shortcode.

ecosystem.mailpoet.install.core.desc.message: Make sure the core plugin is installed and active on your WordPress site.

ecosystem.mailpoet.install.addon.desc.message: Search for "Simple JWT Login MailPoet" on WordPress.org, install, and activate.

ecosystem.mailpoet.install.authCode.desc.message: Go to Simple JWT Login → Auth Codes. Copy the code you want to use for autologin links.

ecosystem.mailpoet.install.template.titl.message: Add the shortcode to your template

ecosystem.mailpoet.install.template.desc.message: Open a MailPoet email template, paste the shortcode with your auth code and desired parameters.

ecosystem.mailpoet.cta.title.message: Turn every email into a one-click login

ecosystem.mailpoet.cta.subtitle.message: Install the free MailPoet add-on, paste one shortcode, and give every subscriber a frictionless path back to your site.

ecosystem.phpSdk.examples.auth.descripti.message: Authenticate any WordPress user by email or username and receive a signed JWT. Pass the token in the Authorization header for all subsequent requests to protected endpoints.

ecosystem.phpSdk.examples.register.descr.message: Register new WordPress users programmatically. Optionally assign a role at creation time and receive a JWT immediately after registration - no admin UI required.

ecosystem.phpSdk.examples.validate.headl.message: Verify a JWT is still valid

ecosystem.phpSdk.examples.validate.descr.message: Check that a token has not expired and its signature matches the plugin decryption key. Use this on every request to protected resources in your application.

ecosystem.phpSdk.examples.refresh.descri.message: Exchange an expiring token for a fresh one without requiring the user to enter credentials again. Perfect for long-running sessions in SPAs and mobile apps.

ecosystem.phpSdk.examples.revoke.descrip.message: Revoke a token so it can never be used again - useful for implementing sign-out, account suspension, or post-deployment security sweeps.

ecosystem.phpSdk.useCases.headless.descr.message: Build a decoupled frontend in Laravel, Symfony, or plain PHP while WordPress handles content. Authenticate users from your PHP app and pass JWTs to the WP REST API.

ecosystem.phpSdk.useCases.registration.d.message: Register users from your own sign-up form and immediately issue a JWT - all in one round trip, without touching the WordPress admin.

ecosystem.phpSdk.useCases.testing.descri.message: Generate tokens in PHPUnit or Pest fixtures to test authenticated flows against a real WordPress instance - no browser, no cookies, no mocking.

ecosystem.phpSdk.meta.title.message: PHP Client SDK - Simple JWT Login

ecosystem.phpSdk.meta.description.message: Official PHP client for Simple JWT Login. Authenticate, register, validate and revoke tokens from any PHP app - one Composer package.

ecosystem.phpSdk.compat.lead.message: The client is a plain PHP library with zero framework dependencies - drop it into Laravel, Yii, CodeIgniter, Symfony, or a standalone script.

ecosystem.phpSdk.api.lead.message: Fluent, chainable API covering authentication, registration, and the full token lifecycle.

ecosystem.phpSdk.useCases.lead.message: From headless WordPress to automated testing - the client handles the auth layer so you can focus on your app.
